answer_text:
Yes. This is a direct consequence of the Hahn–Banach theorem, which says that the continuous dual \(X^*\) separates points of \(X\).

Assume, for contradiction, that \(u \neq 0\). Then \(\|u\|_X > 0\), and we may normalize

\[
v = \frac{u}{\|u\|_X}.
\]

Define a linear functional on the one-dimensional subspace \(\operatorname{span}\{v\}\) by

\[
g(\alpha v) = \alpha.
\]

Then

\[
|g(\alpha v)| = |\alpha| = \|\alpha v\|_X,
\]

so \(\|g\|=1\). By the Hahn–Banach theorem, \(g\) extends to some \(f \in X^*\) with \(\|f\|=1\). Hence

\[
f(v)=1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
f(u)=f(\|u\|_X v)=\|u\|_X f(v)=\|u\|_X > 0.
\]

This contradicts the assumption that \(\langle f,u\rangle = 0\) for every \(f \in X^*\). Thus \(u\) cannot be nonzero, so necessarily \(\|u\|_X=0\).

\[
\boxed{\text{Yes, } \|u\|_X = 0.}
\]
